subject: How to run a prediction model

messages.author: 63f04078443444c3
messages.subject: How to run a prediction model
parts:
Dear ggplotters,

I have a dataset from a cohort of 500 children under
15yrs of age that were screened for measles antibody
titre. Each row in the dataset represents an individual
child. Covariates included in the dataset for each individual are: age, sex,
whether a child ever suffered from measles before (a binary outcome,
yes/no), whether a child ever received measles vaccination before (a
binary outcome, yes/no), observed apparent sign of malnutrition (a binary
outcome, yes/no), and family's socio-economic status (a binary outcome,
low/middle). The level of antibody titre per individual is our dependent
variable and was categorised as 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, and 320. As antibody level
greater or equals to 40 is considered "protective" and anything less as
"unprotective", another dichotomous dependent variable
(protected/unprotected) for level of protection was generated therefrom,
thereby having 2 dependent variables. The antibody titre is an indication
of the level of protection either due to vaccination or natural
infection. My questions are?


1. Should I employ ordinal and logistic regressions in
modelling the categorical antibody titre level (10, 20, 40, 80, 160, and
320) and the dichotomous level of protection (protected/unprotected),
respectively, and thereby produce 2 models from a data with 2 outcomes?


2. As one of my hypothesis is that "measles may
likely increase to 'X' fold in 'Y' year period under this present condition",
how could I run a model on this kind of data to make such
predictions, please?


Many thanks in anticipation of your usual helpful responses.


Kind regards,


Aminu.

messages.author: 463b8c05680be401
messages.subject: Re: How to run a prediction model
parts:
Dear Aminu,

Your questions seem at this stage not really related to ggplot2. I therefore suggest to ask the question at "cross validated" http://stats.stackexchange.com, which aims to provide answers on statistical and methods issues like the ones you present.

Some critical, but intended to be helpful remarks already:
- While I would use ordinal logistic (not linear) regression on the levels of antibody and logistic on the protected/unprotected dependent variable, these are really two very different questions. Are you interested in the different relationships between your independent variables at antibody levels, or do you want to know whether your independent variables are able to explain variance in the protection level.
- Your social-economic status measure is really not helpful. First, if the binary outcome is low vs. middle, you assume there are no children from higher backgrounds in the data (consider using low vs middle and high). But it is also a very crude measure given some of the more widely used class schemes (EGP) or occupational rankings (ISEI, CAMSIS).
- I wonder about your hypothesis indicating that something changes over time? You do not mention that you have time as a variable. If you think of measuring time by the age of the children, please keep in mind that there may cohort effects in effect. (e.g. something in time happening which touches upon the 10-15 year old, but not on the 5-10 year old, such as a government health care budget cut at one point in time, or anti-bodies developing in relation to age-specific hormone-adjustment (puberty).
- Finally, whilst you cannot help it, you should consider what you can derive from your model, given that so many of your variables or dichotomous (binary). It will be very hard to draw conclusions from it on the population.

Kind regards,

Richard
